messages:
Alice: FYI customers report duplicate uploads from our Android quickstart when network flaps. Seeing two identical POSTs to /v1/assets.
Jon: Is this using the streaming RequestBody with progress callbacks?
Alice: Yes. Retrofit + OkHttp, we stream from FileDescriptor so body is not repeatable.
Priya: OkHttp default retryOnConnectionFailure=true can trigger reconnects; with streamed bodies that can cause re-sends.
Will: Repro: run sample on emulator, start upload, toggle airplane mode for ~1.5s, bring network back. Server sees POST, failure, then another POST within seconds.
Alice: Sample log snippet: ```I/okhttp: --> POST https://api.redwood/v1/assets
I/okhttp: --> END POST (streamed)
I/okhttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout
I/okhttp: --> POST https://api.redwood/v1/assets
I/okhttp: --> END POST (streamed)```
Priya: Short-term: change sample client's builder to .retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for upload flows and call out in README. Long-term: SDK should detect non-repeatable bodies and avoid transparent retries.
Jon: Implementation idea: interceptor checks body.contentLength()==-1 or marks RequestBody as OneShot, set request.tag(OneShot::class.java), and have retry logic skip tagged requests.
Will: Also add an emulator integration test that toggles network and asserts only one POST recorded by test server.
ci-bot: CI started for branch fix/dup-upload-sample (build 5122).
Alice: I'll open two PRs: sample change + SDK change. Will include repro script and logs.
